#7664 1 2006-03-26T19:15:57Z Luminaflare
there are 2 to 4 groups in each war and the war is turn based before a war starts I will post the turn order

1) the resistance

2) the red empire

3)

4) GOD a.k.a. me

almost forgot. to sign up you just type in bold join: then 1, 2, 3 or 4 to join the corresponding group for the next war also after you join up post the pic with your base drawn on it and put the stats of you weapons on

RULES:
1) no pictures off the net just hand drawn stuff
2) do not edit the pic till it is your turn
3) you are not allowed to start fighting until the set date and if you don't have a base finsihed and posted by the date you will be placed in an allies base or if you have no allies you will be placed randomly
4) if your gunna move your ninja move it within a reasnable distance(read: not from
one side of the level to the other)
6) you must show where you will attack 1 turn before you do and don't make it some masssive thing just a little suttle thing like the gauss turret targeter will do or if its a rocket put it only part way launched stuff like that (don't use gauss turret targeters make your own up. unless your using a gauss turrent of course)
7) to defend you must wait till your turn also an attack that is set up to hit a target must also wait till the person who started it's turn so like this also that describes the two types of attack instant and air born (instant: lsaer, gun etc. air born: rockets, shurikens etc.)
person 1: fires rocket at person 2
person 2: blows the rocket out of the sky but cannot attack
person 3: fires rocket at person 4
person 4: fires rocket at person 3
person 1: fires rocket at person 4
person 2: aims laser at person 1
person 3: hits person 4 but cannot defend because he needs to finish off a rocket attack
person 4: hits person 3
person 1: aims laser at person 2
person 2: puts up force field to defend against laser

so incase that doesn't make much sense

air borne: takes 2 plus turns to finish can not do anything while attacking with it

instant: takes 1 turn to aim then you can wait a turn to fire it if you want to do something else or you want to charge it up

also there are psychic attacks and those can only be stopped by attacking the attackers base or one of his allies bases also it depends on the type of attack for psychic attacks. the range on psychic attacks is limited to allie bases

8) me and ctb are gods you can try and gain our favour with offerings and whatnot at the temples but if we dont like your offering we may be vengeful

9) if a player is losing badly an event will happen (weapon crate drop, god helps etc.) not neccesserilly good also if the winning team try's to pick up a weapon crate it will blow up)

______________________________________________________________________

background story:
N city was originaly ruled by the Gold King all was good and happy until the red military squad overthrew the Gold King and created the red empire and ninja's who refused to follow the corrupt leader of the empire where killed so the resistance was formed. The God(s) decided to watch and lend a helping hand when appeased. the group was created by the supposedly dead gold king (a gold ninja) and are the remenents of the Gold King and his followers.
______________________________________________________________________

group specials:
1)the resistance: the abilty to recroute members from the red empire
2) the red empire: the abilty to capture and torture aposing forces into working for them
3) : stealth ability can become invisible for 3 turns (use light grey ninja setting on N poser)
4) try and gain my favour with offerings and whatnot but if i dont like your offering i may be vengeful
______________________________________________________________________

I might add more later so keep checking this post also if you think of a rule please post it

I think if the first few games go well I will create a new topic just for playing it and use this one for signing up or the other way around (bit like mafia game)

Come to Alagasia! We have a strong alliance with Exendergarsen, Which has a steady supply of steel, iron, nickel, and oil flowing south, and we also have more than enough Bauxite, magnesium, and sulphur coming out the mines. You will never go hungry in Alagasia as there is always a plentiful supply of fish from the coast. We plan on setting up hospitals, fire stations, and police head quarters dotted all around the country. The two islands to the south will be fitted out with private villas. There are plenty of job opportunities, from working in the factories refining the bauxite and magnesium, to working in the hospitals and shops. Alagasia is out of the way of all those big countries - have you read the history of England, one of the smallest countries on Earth? They had the best Navy around, and was the biggest contributor to winning World Wars 1, 3 and 5, while the USA's massive military force only contributed to World Wars 2 and 4. Also, if you come to Alagasia you will never be bored with all the partying in the town centre at night, the country is bouncing up and down more than a jack rabbit on a pogo stick, we are about to buy the most powerful sub-woofer in all of Collosus and one of the most powerful surround sound systems as well. If you're looking for stuff to buy then you will be able to go to our shopping district, and do you want to watch the intergalactic football? You can get HD tvs cheap in our i-Bay stores, or have you got a need for some firearms? Go to Lucky Joe's Lock Stock and Two and a Half Smoking Barrels Munitions Dump, or do you want to get high? Go to the airosphere - thats twice as good as any dome you'll ever go to - and if you get hungry, why not visit Burger Emperor or McMickeys? Yes, this place is an all around good place to be.

Do you want a dull, boring life? Go to some other country. But if you want a fun, exciting life, come to Alagasia.

Quote: usaswim, May 29, 2007 11:38 pm
1. Never carry too much for too long unless it is necessary.
2. Walk with a sense of purpose. If you are wandering aimlessly or look lost you become a target.
3. Act and dress like a local. Tourists are frequent targets of muggers.
4. Carry a weapon where it is permitted. Pepper spray, a 4 inch lockback pocketknife, or a pistol (9mm or 38 caliber minimum for stopping power) will give you confidence that muggers will sense and steer away from. This of course assumes you know how to use your weapon and are carrying it in such a manner that it is unlikely it can be used against you.
5. Learn a martial art, at least the basics. In cases where weapons are not an option, you need to know you can defend yourself with your hands and feet (and head) if necessary. Your confidence radiates outwards and protects you from feral humans who can sense fear.
6. When you sense danger, don't be afraid to act a little crazy. Walking down the middle of the street, and/or singing a song at the top of your lungs will make you a less attractive target. This contradicts the above advice of "not drawing attention to yourself", but when it seems that the attention is already there, it's time to act to discourage action.
7. Determine the risk factor of you getting mugged or robbed. These are the things that let you outweigh your risk of being robbed.
*
o Clothes: Are you dressed like a rich person? Do you have fancy jewelery? Are you wearing a T-shirt and jeans or a suit?
o What you're carrying: Are your hands empty or are you carrying a briefcase, backpack, or suitcase?
o The area you are in: Is it an urban area with a lot of foot traffic, or a suburban neighborhood with few pedestrians?
o How long you will be traveling: The longer you are on the streets, the higher the odds of you passing by at least one thief.

1) Obviously

2) Some people just look lost no matter what ;_;

3) Nice tip although considering the fact that you wouldn't really go out of town just to get some money it's kinda useless in this situation

4) Illegal in the UK

5) You need a lot of patience which some people just don't have

6) This comes naturally for some people and others would prefer to be mugged than embarrassed (seriously)

7) Common sense (Or it should be)

#16969 1 2007-08-26T23:01:00Z Luminaflare
I just had an idea for a (in my opinion) pretty awesome RPG game.

Here's the premise: It's an online game. 1-3 people join as 'heroes' who choose a class and a name etc. they would have either have a first or third person view (presuming the game is 3D) with keys mapped WASD style with attacks mapped to the mouse with left click for weapon attack and right click for specials (magic, setting traps etc.) with scroll being able to cycle spells.the I key would access a diablo style inventory screen where you can arrange items, equip different ones etc. and other rpg key binds (C for character info, M for skills etc.). the HUD would have health and mana bars along with the currently selected spell icon next to them in an oblivion-esque style. Or it would be a looking down style view like diablo, titan quest etc. with left click as a generic command button (move to that spot, attack monster, open chest, etc.) and right click as a button for using skills, the HUD and key maps would be the same apart from no WASD.

1 player would join as a 'dungeon master' and would have RTS style gameplay and view, being able to set traps in the dungeon, create units and 'spawn them' in to play (out of protaganist site unless the DM builds a 'teleport node' which lets you create units in player site until they destroy it and not where prot have already explored unless they have missed a 'teleport node') they can also edit any floor of the dungeon below the protaganists and empty of players. Treasure chests would be randomly spawned in corridors and side routes built on to the DMs map after creating so as to balance gameplay (in otherwords DMs can't heavily secure chests and stuff it's all done by the computer). The DM gains resources to build units and stuff by killing randomly spawning AI 'heroes' thay try to get through the dungeon (so there is no way to just mindlessly mine resources the DM has to actually work to get them)

1-3 players would also be able to choose to be an antagonist (mainly just negative class choices as the protaganists like dark knight instead of night, neromancer instead of cleric etc.) and essentialy just work the same as the protaganists but these gain experience from killing AI heroes rather than monsters and aim to stop the protaganists. also there would have to be some form of lives or something to stop antagonists and protagonists death matching (perhaps antagonists being restricted to certain depths of the dungeon and starting out more powerful so that they are more like boss characters)

any players after the initial 7 would be able to choose to control any of the monsters that the DM creates and can either fight like smarter monster spam or spend time gaining experience off of AI heroes and gradually becoming 'unique' enemys at level 5 or so where you can name your creature and choose a class (like blood thirster or something) main difference between antagonists is that they start at minimum level and all skills are pre-defined.

---

Well it's midnight so i'll probably expand upon this tommorow currently i'd just like to here comments on this idea, suggestions for what engine to run it in etc.

Also i'd like to see if anyone would be up to coding this and/or help me make the graphics.

Quote: Grassman7z7, August 27, 2007 03:01 am
1: The person building the Dungeon, the DM, would have to be limited in some ways, and rewarded in others.
What if he just made crummy dungeons, where all the "phat lewt" was easy to grab? Then you could just pimp out your character and massacre anything in your path.

2: Obviously, you would want to be able to go to other Dungeons with your Hero, and adventure there. What fun is it for all three parties (Protagonists, Antagonists, and DM) if some dude can hop on the server and totally own everything?

1: Setting a level requirement/limit could help, but you could still easily "twink" your hero by having a friend build a Dungeon filled with chests that you could easily get to.

3: Antagonist would be another problem.
Obviously, you wouldn't want to hang out in a dungeon and wait for people to join so you can be killed by them kill them. You could end up waiting for a long time, and get little reward. AI Heroes would work, but then you have to figure out how you control their power and the like. If it were up to the DM, once again he could power level someone if he was so inclined, and you could dungeon hop (Once again, all that work to (If done so legitimately) level up, you would HAVE to allow players to play on other dungeons).
Although being an antagonist would be fun, developing a fair, balanced game would be extremely tough, and likely easy to exploit.
And what about incentive for people playing as creeps to guard chests, other than the fact that it makes heroes more powerful. Wouldn't they want some sort of reward?

4: So, the best way I can think of to prevent exploitation would be "League" style maps. The only way to be able to Map on these servers would be to have enough kudos and then apply to one of the developers. Then he would judge you, and you would receive "professional" status, and be able to DM these "League" dungeons. Then, you could join these maps (Anyone could) and play, but you cant carry over any characters that aren't from league games. Just to be fair.

5: If the game were to be limited to LAN games, or just on an overall smaller scale, then exploitation would not be an issue. However, finding people would be a pain. Thats where servers come in handy, or something. Theres really a lot that would need to be done for anything like this to become a reality, and unfortunately, I doubt that there are any game developers, publishers, or anyone, who would be willing to work on a project this demanding.

Both of the games were released one year apart, and by associated game developers NaughtyDog (Publishing Jak and Daxter), and Insomniac Games (publishing Ratchet and Clank).
They both feature a main character and a nonhuman sidekick traveling around planets and fighting off large, often egotistically devious bad guys, with slapstick humor along the way.
Both feature platforming and shooter gameplay styles.
Both feature various driven vehicles, upgradeable weapons, near-identical art styles, near-identical gunplay styles, and near-identical animations.
Both feature racing components.
Both have tons of sequels on different platforms.
Both have the sidekick "Saving The Day" at multiple points in the storylines.
NaughtyDog borrowed displacement mapping technology from Insomniac Games, in exchange for pixel-relation technology from NaughtyDog. Both games include these technologies, so both of the games include very nice, albeit very cloned versions of special effects.
Both include monetary systems that are earned by breaking the environments and/or killing enemies.
Both games include generic weapons, such as versions of a shotgun, versions of a machine gun, and melee attacks.
Both games have identical save/load systems.
Both games include at least one female character catching the eye of the male hero; which, in both games, causes the sidekick of the main hero to verbally antagonize or taunt the hero in multiple ways.

Now... which one of these games do you personally prefer?

I'd have to go with Ratchet and Clank - simply because I find it more fun to play.

~Mosh

Bold means wrong, Itallic means ridiculous.

Now here is where i get my gaming discussion hat on.

Now on which is better depends upon which game it is in the series.

Jak and Daxter vs Ratchet and Clank:

Now at the begining J&D was much more platformy than R&C (infact the entire game was based around it no weapons) while R&C and a bit of platforming but had quite a few weapons and required use of them. Now since i prefer shooting to platforming i prefer R&C.

Jak II vs Ratchet and Clank 2: Going Commando/Locked and Loaded

Now we get to the middle point, J2 had introduced guns and vehicles and the entire game seemed to flow very well story wise and gameplay wise and you could get about 2 upgrades for each weapon. In R&C2 weapons were made upgradeable and you could get armour and the gameplay stayed pretty much the same just expanded. Here i liked both games just as much as the other.

Jak 3 vs Ratchet and Clank 3: Up Your Arsenal

The last in the original series of games, J3 stayed pretty much the same as J2. R&C3 was expanded more in making more upgrades to your weapons etc. My opinion stays the same in that i like both games just as much.

Spin offs! (only ones i've played)

Jak X vs Ratchet: Deadlocked/Gladiator

Ah the first 2 spin off games. Jak X... well... Cart racing. Ratched: Deadlocked/Gladiator removes clank from your back and turns the story mode more in to a series of challenges, it expands the weapon upgrades even more adding mods (these may have been added in R&C3 i forget) and giving you 2 upgradeable robot buddys. overall a good game sticking to the spirit of ratchet and clank game. Needless to say i prefer Ratchet: Deadlocked/Gladiator.

So yeah i prefer Ratchet and Clank.

Oh and if i put 2 names either side of a slash that means the game has a different name in the UK rather than america.

#18024 1 2007-11-19T18:17:18Z Luminaflare
Ok so this is my guide to installing software from a disc image without the disc. I presume that you have daemon tools or equivalent virtual drive software installed.

Ok first you need the disc image, i got mine from command and conquers website since they released the first one for free. Ideally you should download it to your desktop for ease of location.

You can see the 2 command and conquer ISO files on my desktop (you need only pay attention to GDI95.iso)


Ok now that you should have iso file for your software of choice you should right click on daemon tools and move the mouse over Virtual CD/DVD-ROM and then over device 0: (it should have the drive letter in square brackets) so you get this menu


Cick on the highlighted menu selection in the picture and then select your disc image as so.


Click Ok/Open and the start screen of the disc should appear, if not try running it from my computer or browsing the CD for the setup file. As you can see my start screen appeared

Short because I have typed out a long post for this twice and both times Opera closed somehow (By annoying keyshortcuts or whatever)

Description ripped from site:
Clonk is an entertaining, action-packed game of strategy, tactics, and skill. It can be played by a single player, with up to four players on one computer, or any number of players in local networks or via internet.

The game is played in realtime rounds in which each player controls his hardy crew of clonks in order to either mine resources and build up a base or eliminate the opponent's crew.

Run-time generated or predefined landscapes feature everything from hills, mountains, lakes, deserts, arctic wastelands to volcanic rocks, islands floating in mid-air or suboceanic terrain. This guarantees a neverending variety of scenarios.


Experience changing weather conditions with rain, snow, thunderstorms, as well as tectonics and hectic animal activity. A unique physics engine allows rain, flowing water, crumbling earth, snow drifts, lakes of lava...

Build new structures using materials you have created in complex production chains. Extend your base and prepare for battle by developing new weapons and tactics.

There is an almost unlimited number of options to customize the game. Experienced players can create their own scenarios and set individual game goals to create new mission objectives.

More advanced players can go even further. Clonk features a powerful and very flexible scripting language with full technical documentation. Want even more? For programmers the full source code of the current official version is publicly available.


Clonk is a strongly community based game. There are thousands of players in Germany and around the world who meet, play, edit, develop, and extend this game every day and have filled the 12-year-history of this project with unceasing activity.

Clonk is international: through community contributions, the language base of the game (more than 20,000 words) has been translated into ten different languages.

The most up-to-date version of Clonk is shareware. You can test the game for free. Extended scenarios or editing features are available with a registration.

Previous versions of the game are freeware and offer a convenient entry (and months of playing fun) at no cost.

ill add to that a game which i greatly dislike: Half Life 2: for being overrated, and great at being average. The story is alright but it isnt exactly revolutinary. Hey cool; you're the first guy I've seen who's criticized HL2 without getting thrown down for a full 10 min. Myself I don't think the guns are anything less than average, the ragdoll and multi-object interaction physics are way better than FEAR IMO, but still that's only opinions. However there's one thing that it'd like to criticize the game for that's hard to mention at most places; it's linearlism (sorry, grammar Nazi's). Whenever you don't know where to go the only thing to do is to walk where you haven't been, since there's not a single square meter that's not along the way. Also it feels a bit stupid when someone's impressed of you finding the right way while in reality you didn't even know why you were going in a certain direction and even less where. Also, if the rebellion outposts are all along the way of an inescapable sewer/canyon/canal/tunnel/wtvr, then how come the combine's incapable to find them? One'd think it was just for them to walk along the way and they'd get at least 20 outposts to wipe out in half an hour.

Having said that, there's another game I'd like to add on the list:
StarCraft: Brood War.
That is probably the worst expansion I've ever seen, removing most of the fun by adding countermeasures for the previus countermeasures followed by counter-countermeasures to counter the glitches created by the countering of the first countermeasures in the first place. Sure, the game's almost to old to be criticised anymore, since there's nothing else from the era that still lives (few exceptions), but I would've been better of without that expansion set. Also, Fenix dies. Why the hell did they let people like arcturus live when my favourite character gets killed by my own hand? I hate you, Blizzard!

I would like to point out HL2 came out before F.E.A.R. and it does have a better physics engine (i'd like to see someone attempt a gmod with F.E.A.R.). Sure the story is a bit meh but so is pretty much every other FPS's story. Sure it's linear but yet again so is pretty much every other fps.

Whe HL2 was released it was ground breaking and after episode 3 i really think valve should pull together and make a Half life 3 (even though the episodes are supposed to be that) so rather than these tiny little update they can make something ground breaking and make everyone go 'Wow' again.

Kinda Halo, I like it but the fanboyism surrounding it annoys me to no end.

Halo was groundbreaking because it was the first FPS on XBOX to have one analog stick for aiming, and one for shooting. The story was great, the vehicles felt like they were naturally part of the environment, it had innovative new weapons and a great single player/co-op storyline. The shield system greatly enhanced gameplay, and was the inspiration for almost every modern FPS (though the first halo did have health). Most good shooters now don't have a health bar, but if you take too many hits in a row you'll drop. True, it isn't the best shooter ever made (Perfect Dark is.), but it's pretty damn far up there. As far as I'm concerned, it was the best thing ever to hit the XBOX.
FPS games on the PS1 did that years before so it's not exactly groundbreaking or inovating. Also i'd like to point out that halo is the first FPS released for the xbox. And yeah there's ntohing wrong with the haloverse i just think the games are mediocre.

I see your point, but I stick to mine. The reason people wanted Halo 3 so bad, according to you, is because it was part of the Halo franchise. Startopia would be my example for your angle. Greatest game ever, but it sold like, 20,000 copies.

Example when Half life came out it sold well because it was groundbreaking and a good shooter at the time. When HL2 came out it sold mostly because people were excited about the sequal do a game they loved and bought it when it came out.

#403298 85 2008-01-23T01:56:37Z Luminaflare
No...

Halo 1-3 aren't bad. Just mediocre.

Now hype is not generated by how good a game is as such since a lot of games that have no games before them are hyped. Hype is more based upon what features the game promises and what they show in their tech demos. There are plenty of game series where the sequal is hyped to hell but turns out to be very mediocre and there are new series that get released that turn out a lot worse than promised.

What I'm trying to say is that games sell on hype but hype is not a measure of a games worth. Example: Assasins Creed got a lot (and i mean ridiculous amounts) of hype and sold well, the game is good but does not live up to all the hype yet it still sold better than it would if they did the marketing on exactly how the game turned out. Marketing sells games not the production team, not the publishers. Marketing.

Also keep in mind I'm criticising the gameplay and hype of teh Halo series nothing else.

Quote
Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars is a real-time strategy video game developed and published by Electronic Arts for the Windows, Mac OS X and Xbox 360 platforms, and was released internationally in March 2007[2]. The direct sequel to the 1999 RTS title Command & Conquer: Tiberian Sun by Westwood Studios, a now defunct company that was taken over and liquidated by EA in 2003, Tiberium Wars returns the Command & Conquer series to its roots in the Tiberium story arc of the franchise, once again featuring the factions of the Global Defense Initiative and the Brotherhood of Nod, and also introducing a new extraterrestrial faction known as the Scrin.

Tiberium Wars takes place in the year 2047, at the advent of and during the "Third Tiberium War" when the Brotherhood of Nod launches a worldwide offensive against the Global Defense Initiative; abruptly ending seventeen years of silence and crippling GDI forces everywhere. With the odds tipped in the Brotherhood's favor this time, GDI field commanders rally their troops and begin to combat Nod's second re-emergence, trying to restore lost hope.

#426768 2 2008-04-10T08:56:08Z Luminaflare
Direct copy paste from my word document for the first character.

Character Ideas:

Name: Chad Exoskeleton Kinghorn

Personality: Is not very social, feels at home with technology. Prefers machines to people (Yes I realise this is the same as what I just said). He is actually extremely intelligent.

Appearance: Medium length, dishevelled brown hair. Always wears jeans, a T-shirt, fingerless leather gloves, sneakers and a pair of glasses on his forehead which he uses when working.

Power(s): Robotic suit that he calls his Exoskeleton.

Starts out as Exoskeleton-Prototype which is simply just the most basic parts of his suit linked together with hydraulics to increase his strength, there is little or no armour plating. It is simply polished steel without any colouring apart from the suits name etched on to the backpack portion. The suit consists of a torso piece which serves as armour plating for his chest and backpack piece which serves to give him flight via Angel Wings (They look like 3 lengths of rectangular metal with a single booster on the first piece which is connected to the suit and 2 boosters on the next 2 pieces, the wings fold up in to the backpack piece when not in use. Named Angel Wings because the white flame of the boosters make them look like an Angels wings when In use), boots which have small boosters on the bottom for stability in flight among other uses (Jumping higher etc.), a pair of gauntlets which he mainly uses for protecting his hands, a headband like helmet with a visor on the front which he uses for scanning the area and getting feedback on his suit and has armour pieces at each joint to protect the machinery (Knees, shoulders, elbows, waist). With this he also uses a large railgun rifle which has a VS (Virtual Scope) which interacts with his helmet so he can aim as if hes looking through a scope without actually having to lift the weapon up to his head.

The second version is called Exoskeleton-beta It has a dark brown metallic colour to it, has the suits named etched on it and looks more professionally made in general. The entire suit is now armoured, the helmet now covers the entire head but the face is not armoured and is simply covered in the same material of the original visor (It now gives vitals, has improved scanning systems and is easier to make sense of), the flight systems on the back have been improved (As well as looking more well made there are now 4 wings instead of 2), the stabilising boosters on the boots have been improved and now allow him to seemingly hover for a short period of time. The gauntlets now have a low powered laser placed between the middle 2 knuckles and have a high voltage panel in the centre of the palm that can be turned on and off to give foes electric shocks varying from a small shock to stun or a large one to kill. The railgun has been improved to fire the metal longer and further, the metal slugs have been improved from a simple metal pole to an aero-dynamic spike for increased penetration and the VS has been improved to highlight known vital areas, night vision and thermal vision and to distinguish between friend and foe (Via small electrical devices on friends). As well as the improved railgun 2 small hand held firearms have been developed that magnetically attach to the armour so he can place them anywhere, the work like miniature versions of the original railgun except the VS now only highlights foes but has the night vision and thermal vision added to it.



The third version is reconfigurable so has 3 names for its 3 main modes, these are Exoskeleton-Delta, Exoskeleton-Epsilon and Exoskeleton-Gamma.

Delta is Black and Red in colour and has a demonic look to it and is configured for being in the middle of the action and brawling so it has more armour, boosters equipped to parts of the armour to increase the speed at which he can hit and a fully armoured helmet with a small visor which has VS built in due to having no firearms, the angel wings are now called Demon Wings there are still 4 but the booster colour is now blackish-red in colour and the position has been reconfigured to be in an X shape on his back. All boosters are now Blackish-red in colour and have a heavily increased amount of thrust for the sacrifice of being able to use them for more than a short period of time apart from the boosters on the bottom of the boots which have been configured to allow him to use a quick short bust or a longer boost used to hover which paired with the new Demon Wings allows him to fly in to battle at a very fast speed.

Epsilon is white and light blue in colour and has a smoother has an angelic look to the armour, the helmet sticks with the full face visor from beta but also gives vitals of anything that is in its sights, it is configured for ranged support, it has increased the amount of Angel Wings from 4 to 6 for improved flight, it forgoes all railgun based systems for energy based weaponry with a very large laser bombardment cannons mounted to the shoulders which fold over on to the back when not in use and can be used for quick speed boosts in flight. The lasers on the gauntlets have been improved and the boosters on the boots have been removed. The railgun has been replaced with a laser rifle which has an extremely large range and the VS has been improved to reflect this. The mini-railguns have been replaced with laser pistols which fire faster and are more accurate the VS has been improved on these to show places where the guns could cause an environmental attack (Melting the chain holding a girder up etc.). The boosters on Epsilon are all pure white and the lasers are all light blue. The suit is also equipped with medical technology.

Gamma has the same polished steel of the prototype and is configured for medium range combat with improved railgun technology. The only differences between this and beta slightly more armour (the armour on the helmet now covers the entire face apart from the headband shape across the eyes which makes it look like the prototype helmet with armour, the railguns can now change the metal slugs before firing (For example charging them with electricity, heating them up etc.) and have an improved firing mechanism for further increased range, speed and reload time, an auto-reloaded also increases the reload time allowing for fairly rapid fire, the VS on all 3 weapons is now equipped with thermal and sonic x-ray as well (Can see heat and sound signatures through objects). The lasers on the gauntlets have also been removed.

All versions of the suit after beta have respirators equipped so he can breath anywhere apart from a total vacuum. The next version of the armour will be called omega and essentially be a combination of Delta, Epsilon and Gamma. Major difference between lasers and railguns is the way they deal damage, lasers use energy which more burns things away on the surface and gradually cuts through things (Although when I say gradually it can be quite fast) where as railguns fire metal slugs at high speed which simply rips through objects allowing you to fire through objects.)
